actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Accepted for the class contract; a MuJoCo reset restores the model defaults (mj_resetData) and does not use a seed
inputs.name: seed

facts.text: The README describes the repository as 'Simulator of UR5 robotic arm with Roboriq gripper, built with MuJoJo'
The README requires MuJoCo 1.5.0 and mujoco-py
The README's Python usage is 'from environment import lab_env'
The lab_env constructor loads xmls/lab_env.xml as the real-world simulator and xmls/light_env.xml to locate the gripper
The upstream reset writes 42 qpos values from initial_pos and then overwrites the first three with the selected task's joint_pos values

The upstream step maps action[0], action[1] and action[2] to qpos[0], qpos[1] and qpos[2] over -30 to 45 degrees, -105 to -50 degrees and 0 to 180 degrees, and uses action[3] for the number of gripper closing steps

The upstream get_state renders 960 by 720 images from workbench_camera and upper_camera, crops 214 by 214 windows, adds Gaussian noise, and returns the two images plus the six-element vector [x1, y1, x2, y2, grasped, danger]
The upstream safety_check steps the simulation, sums the absolute movement of the first six joints and compares it with safety_threshold
The safety_threshold is 0.01
The model root element is '<mujoco model="ur5">' and its compiler element declares angle radian and meshdir meshes
The option element sets gravity 0 0 0, an elliptic cone and timestep 0.02 s
The global default class gives joints frictionloss 1 and damping 1 and motors gear 0.8
The arm is a chain of six hinge joints named joint1 to joint6
The right gripper finger has hinge joints joint7_1 with range 0 to 0.872664626 rad, joint8_1 and joint9_1 with range 0 to 2.967059728 rad, and joint10_1 with range 0 to 1 rad
The left gripper finger has hinge joints joint7_2 with range 0 to 0.872664626 rad, joint8_2 and joint9_2 with range 0 to 2.967059728 rad, and joint10_2 with range 0 to 1 rad
Four target bodies each declare three slide joints free_x, free_y and free_z and one ball joint free_ball

The actuator section declares twelve motor actuators: gravity_1 to gravity_4 on free_z_1 to free_z_4 with gear '1 0 0 0 0 0', close_1 and close_2 on joint7_1 and joint7_2 with gear '0.2 0 0 0 0 0', joint1_motor with gear 1.2, and joint2_motor to joint6_motor
No active actuator element of the model declares a ctrlrange attribute
The model declares the cameras workbench_camera and upper_camera
The model declares four touch sensors on target_site_1 to target_site_4

determinism.notes: MuJoCo integrates one model deterministically from one initial state; the bridge takes no working seed input and cap.world.reset.v1 restores the model defaults, so a run repeats on the same engine but no seed selects a different state.  The package's fake is deterministic too, but its placeholder motion is not the engine's physics

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it parses the model for the joint dimensions, the actuator count, the control targets and the absent ctrlrange, but integrates a placeholder first-order motion and resolves no contact, equality, tendon, mesh, texture, sensor or camera

the upstream environment.py task interface is NOT COVERED: its reset applies initial_pos (:16-23) and joint_pos (:24-27, :89-92), its step maps a four-element action to three joint angles and a gripper sequence (:103-141), and get_state returns two cropped noisy 214 by 214 camera images plus the grasp/danger vector (:170-188); the MuJoCo bridge instead exposes mj_resetData/mj_step and the model integration state, so the camera arrays and the task-level outputs are not served

the model declares no actuator ctrlrange (xmls/lab_env.xml:232-243), so the bridge publishes action.ctrl operator_required: a step that sets it is refused until the site's site-limits.json bounds it, and site-limits.example.json is operator example data, not a model bound; the values are simulated controls in the model's units and nothing was validated against a real UR5 or Robotiq gripper
MuJoCo itself was not importable where the gate ran, so no trajectory of this package was compared with the real engine, and the sim backend that imports mujoco was not run

measures.description: Declared native checkpoint. Integration profile restores the full native input vector; basic profile restores only advertised state plus actuator activation and exact native time. Neither profile certifies external callbacks, plugins, RNG or hardware fidelity.
measures.name: native_checkpoint

operator_required.name: step
operator_required.reason: the model gives none of its actuators no control range (ctrllimited false or no ctrlrange), so MuJoCo leaves the control unclamped; site-limits.json must bound action.ctrl before a step can set it

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch, and the integration state is kept and stays readable
